answer: In a market where agents monitor vine health, each identity must lock $100 for 30 days before it can bid on jobs. A public randomness beacon assigns eligible identities to jobs, with one ticket per bond. Creating 10,000 identities therefore ties up $1 million for a month; splitting one deposit across aliases earns no extra tickets. A sybil spiral remains possible, but its scale is limited by capital the attacker must keep idle.
